questions.title: Why can you compress a gas?
opts: The gas particles are far apart, so they can move closer; the liquid particles already touch.
The gas particles are smaller, so more of them fit into the space when you push the lid.
The gas particles are soft, so they change shape; the liquid particles are hard, so they cannot.
The liquid particles stay still, so nothing can push them closer, but the gas particles move.

questions.title: Gaps between rails
opts: On hot days the rails expand, so the gaps stop them pushing into each other and bending.
The gaps let rainwater flow away from the rails, so the metal does not rust in wet weather.
On cold days the rails expand, so the gaps stop the cold metal from breaking into pieces.
The gaps make each rail lighter and cheaper, so trains can travel along the track faster.

questions.title: Pouring water
opts: Its shape changes, but its volume stays 100 cm³.
Its shape and its volume both change.
Its shape stays the same, but its volume gets bigger.
Its volume gets smaller, because the bowl is much wider.

questions.title: A misty mirror
opts: Condensing: water vapour in the air cools on the mirror and becomes a liquid.
Evaporating: liquid water on the mirror gains energy and becomes water vapour.
Freezing: liquid water on the mirror loses energy and becomes solid ice.
Deposition: water vapour in the air loses energy and becomes solid ice directly.

questions.title: Ice in a freezer
opts: Deposition
Condensing
Freezing
Sublimation

questions.title: Solid, liquid or gas at room temperature?
Nitrogen gas
opts: An element: its molecules have only one type of atom.
A compound: its atoms are joined by a bond.
A mixture: it has two atoms in each particle.
A compound: it has more than one atom in each molecule.

questions.title: Iron sulfide and a magnet
opts: The iron and sulfur reacted to make a new substance, iron sulfide, with new properties.
The heat destroyed all of the iron atoms, so there is no iron left in the test tube.
The yellow sulfur covers each piece of iron, so the magnet cannot reach the iron.
Heating a metal removes its properties for ever, so hot iron is never magnetic again.

questions.title: Which must be true?
opts: A compound made of ions, such as salt, has two or more different elements.
Every particle made of two or more atoms joined together is a compound.
Every compound is made of molecules, each with two or more atoms joined.
A substance made of molecules must be a compound of different elements.

questions.title: Which one is a suspension?
opts: B, chalk in water: it is cloudy, and the chalk settles when it is left to stand.
A, copper sulfate in water: it has a blue colour, so it must have solid pieces in it.
C, milk in water: it is cloudy, so its pieces must settle when it is left to stand.
All three: every mixture settles to the bottom when it is left to stand long enough.

questions.title: The torch beam (extension)
opts: Its droplets of fat are big enough to scatter light; dissolved particles are too small.
Copper sulfate absorbs all of the light, so no beam can pass through the blue solution.
Milky water is a solution, and a beam of light is always seen inside a solution.
The torch shines more brightly on the milk than on the copper sulfate solution.

questions.title: Read the graph: 15 g of salt
What the graph shows
opts: The more salt is dissolved, the lower the freezing point of the water.
The more salt is dissolved, the higher the freezing point of the water.
Salt does not change the freezing point of the water at all.
Water with salt in it still freezes at 0 °C, like pure water.

questions.title: Which glass is more concentrated?
opts: Glass B is more concentrated: it has more solute particles in the same volume.
Glass A is more concentrated: its solute particles have more space between them.
They are equally concentrated, because the two glasses hold the same volume.
Glass B is more dilute, because it has more solute particles in the same glass.

questions.title: Too strong
opts: Add more water to the same glass of drink.
Add more drink powder to the same glass.
Heat it until some of the water evaporates.
Put it in the fridge to make it much colder.

questions.title: Choosing a remover
opts: Propanone
Ethyl ethanoate
Ethanol
Water

questions.title: Oil and water
opts: A separating funnel: oil is less dense, so the water flows through the tap first.
Filtration: the oil particles are too big to pass through the holes in the filter paper.
A magnet: the water is attracted to the magnet, but the oil stays where it is.
Evaporation: the oil evaporates when it is heated, and only pure water remains.

questions.title: Where does the bead stop?
opts: On top of the honey: denser than the other three liquids, less dense than honey.
On top of the oil: it is a solid, and a solid object always floats on any liquid.
At the very bottom: it is a solid, and a solid object always sinks in any liquid.
On top of the water: it is less dense than water but denser than the oil.

questions.title: A pencil start line (extension)
opts: Pencil is insoluble in the solvent, so the line stays where it is.
Pencil lines are darker than ink, so the dyes travel further up the paper.
Pencil helps the solvent rise through the paper more quickly.
Ink lines are too thin to see once the paper is wet with solvent.

questions.title: The brown sweet
opts: Yellow (E102), red (E129) and blue (E133)
Yellow (E102) and blue (E133), but no red
Red (E129) and blue (E133), but no yellow
Yellow (E102) and red (E129), but no blue

questions.title: Sweet or drink?
opts: No: the drink has a pink spot that the sweet does not have, so the dyes differ.
Yes: the sweet and the drink both look orange, so they must have the same dyes.
Yes: both have a yellow spot at the same height, so all their dyes are the same.
No: the sweet has more spots than the drink, so the sweet has an extra dye.
